Steph scored \(15\) baskets out of \(20\) attempts in the first half of a game, and \(10\) baskets out of \(10\) attempts in the second half. Candace took \(12\) attempts in the first half and \(18\) attempts in the second. In each half, Steph scored a higher percentage of baskets than Candace. Surprisingly they ended with the same overall percentage of baskets scored. How many more baskets did Candace score in the second half than in the first?

[Figure 1](attached-image-1)

A bus takes \(2\) minutes to drive from one stop to the next, and waits \(1\) minute at each stop to let passengers board. Zia takes \(5\) minutes to walk from one bus stop to the next. As Zia reaches a bus stop, if the bus is at the previous stop or has already left the previous stop, then she will wait for the bus. Otherwise she will start walking toward the next stop. Suppose the bus and Zia start at the same time toward the library, with the bus \(3\) stops behind. After how many minutes will Zia board the bus?

[Figure 1](attached-image-2)

A \(\bigtriangleup\) or \(\bigcirc\) is placed in each of the nine squares in a \(3 \times 3\) grid. Shown below is a sample configuration with three \(\bigtriangleup\)’s in a line.

[Figure 1](attached-image-3)

How many configurations will have three \(\bigtriangleup\)’s in a line and three \(\bigcirc\)’s in a line?

The figure below shows a polygon \(ABCDEFGH,\) consisting of rectangles and right triangles. When cut out and folded on the dotted lines, the polygon forms a triangular prism. Suppose that:

\[ AH = EF = 8 \]

and

\[ GH = 14. \]

What is the volume of the prism?

[Figure 1](attached-image-4)

A cricket randomly hops between \(4\) leaves, on each turn hopping to one of the other \(3\) leaves with equal probability. After \(4\) hops, what is the probability that the cricket has returned to the leaf where it started?

[Figure 1](attached-image-5)

A square of area \(2\) is inscribed in a square of area \(3,\) creating four congruent triangles, as shown below. What is the ratio of the shorter leg to the longer leg in the shaded right triangle?

[Figure 1](attached-image-6)

An even number of circles are nested, starting with a radius of \(1\) and increasing by \(1\) each time, all sharing a common point. The region between every other circle is shaded, starting with the region inside the circle of radius \(2\) but outside the circle of radius \(1.\) An example showing \(8\) circles is displayed below. What is the least number of circles needed to make the total shaded area at least \(2023\pi?\)

[Figure 1](attached-image-7)

Each square in a \(3 \times 3\) grid of squares is colored red, white, blue, or green so that every \(2 \times 2\) square contains one square of each color. One such coloring is shown on the right below. How many different colorings are possible?

[Figure 1](attached-image-8)

mappings.rationale: Each shaded band is the difference of two nested disk areas, regardless of their different centers. These band areas form an arithmetic sequence; its sum must meet the stated threshold with an even circle count.
mappings.answerReason: With 2m circles, the kth shaded band has area π[(2k)²-(2k-1)²]=(4k-1)π. The total is m(2m+1)π. At m=31 this is 1953π, while at m=32 it is 2080π. Since each additional band has positive area, the least qualifying count is 2×32=64.

mappings.rationale: Apply the four-distinct-colors restriction to overlapping 2×2 blocks. An initial block has 4! arrangements, and compatibility of the remaining blocks determines the number of extensions.
mappings.answerReason: Fix the upper-left block as (a,b;c,d), with all four colors distinct. The upper two cells of the right column must be (a,c) or (c,a), while the left two cells of the bottom row must be (a,b) or (b,a). Of these four pairings, one repeats a in the bottom-right block and is invalid. Each other pairing forces its final cell. Hence there are 4!×3=72 colorings.
